newsitem.title: MEXICO: Santander says Mexico buy part of Latam strategy. [CORRECTED 00:56 GMT 25/10]
newsitem.headline: Santander says Mexico buy part of Latam strategy. [CORRECTED 00:56 GMT 25/10]

text.p: Banco Santander's acquisition of Mexico's Invermexico financial group was its fourth such buy as part of a $2 billion Latin American investment program, a company executive said on Thursday.

"This is another step in Santander's long-term strategy. It was in Mexico that the bank opened its first office outside Spain, in 1950," said Santander board member Ana Patricia Botin during the bank's announcement that it taken control of Grupo Financiero Invermexico (GFInver).

Santander acquired a 75 percent stake in GFInver after a fresh capital injection of $378.5 million (corrects from $371.75 million), and sale of $2.364 billion to the governments Fobaproa bank support fund.
"Our total capital investment in Latin America will be $1.9 billion after this transaction, which is still less than 20 percent of in-house funds we have for investment," Botin said.
Santander already owns banks in Puerto Rico, Peru and Chile, and has expressed an interest in acquiring banks in Colombia and Venezuela.
"We are looking into other possibilities in other countries," Botin added.
